1.pericope_label: The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah
debates: Which town the surname points to, and whether it is a town at all
Whether the summons is to the whole world or only to one land
Whether the holy temple means heaven or the building at Jerusalem
outliers: Gill reports a version making the word a father name rather than a place, and refuses it
Calvin infers the prophet knowledge of his hearers from the pitch of his opening, since mildness would have served a teachable people
Ellicott reads the threefold Hear ye as the structural seam of the whole book
themes: A village named so that anyone could go and ask
Two prophets of one name a century and a half apart
A crier calling a court to silence
Senseless creatures summoned as witnesses

3.pericope_label: For, behold, the LORD cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth
debates: Whether the place God comes out of is heaven or the temple
Whether the melted mountains are hills or kingdoms
Which of the two similes belongs to which half of the verse
outliers: Calvin rejects the reading that makes this God abandoning his temple, and turns it into God leaving the temple to take the bench
Ellicott reports a writer who traces the imagery to a recorded earthquake rather than to the giving of the law
Calvin says an old version reversed the two similes because it could not see how they were arranged
themes: A throne of mercy exchanged for a throne of judgment
A conqueror levelling hills that other armies level by hand
Ground reeling to and fro like a drunkard
A verb used of water, of hatching, and of daybreak

5.pericope_label: For the transgression of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria?
debates: Whether the question asks what the sin is or who is behind it
Whether the cities are named as the offence itself or as its source
Whether the sin reproved here is crime or corrupted worship
outliers: Calvin takes the question as quoted from the hypocrites own mouths and turned back on them
Wesley reads the interrogative as who rather than what, making the capitals the spring of the offence
Calvin distinguishes a kingdom wholly degenerate from one keeping a form of religion with a mixture in it, and gives both the same sentence
themes: A charge laid so that no corner can plead exemption
Rulers whose diseases spread downward, not upward
A capital that thinks itself safe while the country burns
Worship laboriously offered and counted as nothing

6.pericope_label: Therefore I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley
debates: Whether the heap is cleared stones, planting hillocks, or the old vineyard returning
Whether the hire is literal temple prostitution or the figure of spiritual harlotry
What exactly the anger falls on when idols are named
outliers: Ellicott dates the reversal precisely, to the condition of the hill before it was sold to the founder of the dynasty
Clarke takes the hire as actual money earned by women at the temples and spent on its fittings
Calvin says God is not angry with wood and stone but with the abuse of them
themes: Stones cleared from a field and thrown into a corner
A capital returning to the vineyard it was built on
Gold stripped from one set of gods to adorn another
A new form of worship devised to secure a throne

8.pericope_label: Therefore I will wail and howl, I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like the dragons, and mourning as the owls
debates: Whether the word means incurable or simply full of grief
Whether the prophet grief is assumed for effect or actually felt
Whether the capital is reached by the blow or spared
outliers: Calvin rejects the rendering incurable as not suiting the place, against the other four voices
Calvin defends a singular reading held by only two manuscripts, on the grammar of the words around it
Henry says the prophets dreaded the day they announced more than anyone, and mourned to prove it
themes: A funeral procession for a kingdom
A prophet going about like a man out of his senses
Jackals and ostriches chosen for the noises they make at night
Gates that stop an army and gates that do not

10.pericope_label: Declare ye it not at Gath, weep ye not at all: in the house of Aphrah roll thyself in the dust
debates: Why silence is commanded about a disaster nobody could hide
Whether a town name has dropped out of the second clause
Whose standing is taken away in the last clause
outliers: Ellicott recovers a place name by restoring one lost letter, and finds an old Greek version already reading it so
Calvin turns each town name against its bearer, the splendid city stripped and the town named for removing unable to move
Calvin explains the order of silence as a feeling rather than a possibility
themes: News that cannot be hidden but is still not to be told
A wish to perish out of the enemy sight
Rolling in dust in the house of dust
A town named for traffic that dare not stir

12.pericope_label: For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem
debates: Whether the townsmen grieved for good or waited for it in vain
What animal the chariot is to be bound to
Why one border town is called the beginning of sin
outliers: Calvin allows both senses of the verb and prefers the one he did not begin with
Gill collects the natural history of the dromedary, a hundred miles a day against a camel thirty
Ellicott traces the whole charge to the town position on the frontier
themes: A town promised good and given the reverse
A capital spared by an angel while its neighbours were not
A flying camel that runs as a bird flies
Contagion entering at a border and creeping inward

14.pericope_label: Therefore shalt thou give presents to Moresheth-gath: the houses of Achzib shall be a lie to the kings of Israel
debates: Whether the presents are tribute to allies or a bill of divorce
Whether the bald bird is a moulting eagle or a vulture
Which captivity the closing verse describes
outliers: Ellicott turns the gift clause into a dismissal, on a word that can mean either a dowry or a divorce
Calvin says the run of wordplay here is unparalleled anywhere else in the prophets
Clarke admits the closing verses refer to events no historical book records, so their meaning can only be conjectured
themes: A town whose name means lie, and proves one
A prophet naming his own birthplace in the list
An inheritance with an heir who takes by force
Delicate children whose delicacies were a mercy
